title: A child tax allowance
headline: A child tax allowance from 2028-29: Onward, costs £4.8bn a year.
description: Onward proposes a basic-rate child tax allowance: £10,000 of income free of basic-rate tax for a child under five, £20,000 for two and £30,000 for three or more, which parents can split between them. It costs £4.8 billion a year on Onward’s estimate, assuming every couple splits it in the most tax-efficient way. Onward frames it as family support in place of the triple lock’s generosity to pensioners. Held flat in cash.

baselinePolicy.text: Income tax is charged individually with no allowance for children; support for families comes through child benefit and universal credit.

source.quote: the structure of taxation itself remains almost entirely individualised

alreadyIncludes: Child benefit at £27.05 and £17.90 a week and its high-income charge.

earliestStart.text: A new allowance needs Finance Bill legislation and PAYE and self-assessment systems; on the usual sixteen-month Budget timetable a measure announced in October 2026 first applies in 2028-29.

sources.quote: The usual Budget timetable is sixteen months between a Budget announcement and legislation applying from the start of the next tax year
We propose a basic rate Child Tax Allowance of £10,000 per child aged under five

terms.label: Onward’s cost of a basic-rate child tax allowance for children under five, as a cost

source.quote: We estimate this policy would cost £4.8 billion a year, assuming that every two-parent household opts to split the Allowance between them in a tax efficient manner.

rawSource.note: Onward’s figure held flat in cash from the start year; the child population and the tax base would move it. Nobody in government has costed it. Nothing is counted before 2028-29: see earliestStart.

caveats: Onward’s own estimate, with no stated year; it assumes every couple uses the allowance in the most tax-efficient way, which is the upper end of the cost.
Under-fives only, at the basic rate: a family with no basic-rate liability gets nothing from it, so the poorest families gain least.
A tax cut for families with young children rather than a rise; it widens the gap the rest of this Budget has to close.

considerations.text: Working parents of under-fives who pay basic-rate tax, up to £2,000 a year for one child; families below the personal allowance gain nothing, and Onward pairs it with reform of the triple lock.

sources.quote: We propose a basic rate Child Tax Allowance of £10,000 per child aged under five

considerations.text: A transferable allowance needs HMRC to know who the children live with and how the couple has split it, machinery the marriage allowance already runs on a smaller scale.

sources.quote: Parents or primary caregivers would be able to choose to split the Allowance between themselves or have it applied to one income only.

interactions.text: Both move the amount of income a parent can earn before basic-rate tax.
